cell_units: Each tile has 20 by 20 half-square cells; the conventional printed grid is 10 by 10 squares.
rule: Walls are always present at boundaries of rooms, except for explicit doors. Carve named orthogonal routes separately. Reject any room-corridor overlap and any accidental boundary openings. 4 and 15 are rotation invariant: 19-4=15. Rooms may use a rectangular 4-number footprint or contiguous run-length rows [y,xStart,xEnd].

tiles.title: Cloister of Salt
tiles.description: A ritual circuit surrounding an obstructed brine court, with a locked north reliquary and concealed west chapel.

tiles.title: Postern Bastion
tiles.description: Multiple bypass corridors surround a defended gate and magazine complex.

tiles.title: Bone Galleries
tiles.description: Multiple funerary galleries with alternate approaches to the royal sepulcher.

tiles.title: The Basalt Rift
tiles.description: Fault-cut grotto with a flood chamber, hidden connection, and shrine reached by alternative passages.

tiles.title: The Sunken Orrery
tiles.description: An octagonal mechanism court within a service ring, with a hidden choir and sealed chart vault.

tiles.title: The Riftwater Lock
tiles.description: Abandoned floodworks: a six-cell upstream turbine pool meets a three-shutter bank above a receiving sump; the center gate admits a three-cell surge. The canal is sealed against neighboring pedestrian corridors. Its upstream intake adit and downstream tailrace are labeled but continue beyond the mapped level, not invented as surveyed passages. Three handwheels occupy the dry south operating gallery. A dry lower bridge, independent overhead gantry and two inspection circuits offer alternate crossings.
